_note: Gallery page. Behkooshan stone in finished projects, and the quarries.
Each image's `alt` is its caption: the lightbox prints the same line it hands a
screen reader. One line per photograph, in the register of a catalogue plate,
naming what the stone is doing and then what the stone is. Two texts would be
two things to keep in step, and the second one always drifts into marketing.
`cells` is the bento grid in reading order, and auto placement lays it out from
the spans. `span` is columns by rows at the four column width; gallery.css
clamps both down as the grid narrows. The spans below fill four columns exactly,
with no hole, so check that still holds before changing one.
A `shape` cell is a green panel carrying one brand silhouette bleeding off its
edge, which is the only way the stationery ever uses a shape. They carry no text
and are hidden from screen readers. Two of them break up a run of seven
photographs; more would turn punctuation into pattern.
